title: The Disappearing Diamond Stylus
crime_description: The audiophile lounge's $5,000 turntable diamond needle was swapped with a sharpened safety pin.

dossier.text: Security footage at 10:45 PM shows the suspect's hands replacing the diamond needle with a safety pin.
A security camera captures a glimpse of the suspect's pocket watch, which reads 10:45 PM, at the crime scene.
A patron reported seeing the suspect examining the turntable's tonearm at 10:30 PM, about 15 minutes before the crime.

truth_timeline.event: Prof. Fizzypop prepares a set of lockpicks and a spare safety pin.
Prof. Fizzypop swaps the diamond needle with a safety pin.
Prof. Fizzypop flees the scene, accidentally dropping a set of lockpicks.

lie_plan.cover_story: I was in the back room, fixing a wonky pinball machine, and didn't notice anything suspicious.

weak_points.claim: I've never been to the Vinyl & Velvet in my life.
weak_points.planned_slip: Slip statement: 'Actually, I've been there three times already this month.'

weak_points.claim: The pocket watch I'm seen wearing is a family heirloom, and it's not actually a working timepiece.
weak_points.planned_slip: Slip statement: 'Oh, this old thing? It's just a fancy paperweight.'

weak_points.claim: The patron who reported seeing me examining the turntable's tonearm must have mistaken me for someone else.
weak_points.planned_slip: Slip statement: 'What patron? I don't know anyone who works here.'

solution_contradictions: Prof. Fizzypop claimed to have never been to the Vinyl & Velvet, which directly conflicts with fact-1.
Prof. Fizzypop claimed the pocket watch he's seen wearing is a family heirloom and not a working timepiece, which directly conflicts with fact-2.
